issue.title: Find whether any RT grid between 81 and 101 points holds 1e-12 at D 60

milestone.title: G8 · Other paths
milestone.description: Alternatives to our formulation and methods (the RT variables of arXiv:2611.07007, Fourier speed, low D from first principles), the large-D expansion to higher orders, and the complex scalar.

issue.body:
**What.** Solve the RT prototype on grids between 81 and 101 Chebyshev points (85, 91, 95) at D = 55 and 60, each from two starts, against hp's Δ. Recommended by #145's subagent.

**Why.** On 32 × 101, Δ misses 1e-12 at D 60 (−1.27e-12, a second root −2.33e-12), and every finer grid misses by more. The best N falls with D, from at least 141 at D 35 to 101 from D 45. This decides whether any N holds 1e-12 at D 60.

**Acceptance (can fail).** A table of Δ_RT − Δ_hp and the two-root spread for each grid and D, and the verdict on whether any grid holds 1e-12 at D 60.

**Depends on.** #145.

comments.body: started: Mac (Apple M5), a subagent of the coordinator. Checkout: worktree agent-a3f8a38336503b3e7 at main b4d401f (branch wip/i164 for any code or notes). Threads: at most 2 processes at once under nice 10, each one arb thread and two BLAS threads. Raw output: folder I164-mac/ of choptuik-large-d-raw. The criteria go into I164-mac/README.md before the main runs.

Progress, 2026-11-08 13:46 UTC (Mac).

The criteria are in `I164-mac/README.md` (raw commit c1f1669, pushed before the main runs). The D 60.001952 re-solves on 32x85, 32x91 and 32x95 are done, from both starts (a: I145's 32x101 state, b: I145's 32x121 root, each resampled). Every solve converged in 4 to 7 Newton steps.

| grid | Δ_RT − Δ_hp, start a | Δ_RT − Δ_hp, start b | spread of the two roots | `rt_grids.py --tol 1e-12` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32x85 | −3.42e-11 | −3.42e-11 | 1.0e-15 | exit 1 |
| 32x91 | −8.37e-12 | −8.37e-12 | 2.3e-15 | exit 1 |
| 32x95 | −6.38e-13 | −5.85e-13 | 5.4e-14 | exit 0 |
| 32x101 (#145) | −1.27e-12 | −2.33e-12 | 1.1e-12 | exit 1 |

The first column of numbers is the difference to hp's double-double row (up13, err 2e-15). The spread is |Δ_a − Δ_b|, a lower bound on how far the grid leaves Δ undetermined, not an error bar.

So far 32x95 holds 1e-12 at D 60 by the criterion, with both roots inside it. E is not monotone in N (95 is below 101), so by the rule written beforehand 87, 89, 93 and 97 now run at both D from both starts, then 48x95 at D 60 and the `--mutate=coef` control on 32x91. The D 54.996085 runs are under way. 32x85 is already 1.9e-10 off there, larger than at D 60.

Raw commit b7e93b2. cpu: load 4.75, 47% idle; memory: 31G used, 13G compressor; two RT processes, each about 1.3 GB.

Progress, 2026-11-08 14:04 UTC (Mac).

D 60.001952 is done on 85, 89, 91, 93, 95 and 97 from both starts, D 54.996085 on 85, 91 and 95. Every solve converged. Values are Δ_RT − Δ_hp (hp's double-double row, err 2e-15), and the spread is |Δ_a − Δ_b| of the two roots.

| grid | D 60, start a | D 60, start b | D 60 spread | D 55, start a | D 55, start b |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32x85 | −3.42e-11 | −3.42e-11 | 1.0e-15 | +1.89e-10 | +1.89e-10 |
| 32x89 | running | +2.51e-11 | | queued | queued |
| 32x91 | −8.37e-12 | −8.37e-12 | 2.3e-15 | −8.32e-12 | −8.32e-12 |
| 32x93 | +2.35e-12 | +2.81e-12 | 4.6e-13 | queued | queued |
| 32x95 | −6.38e-13 | −5.85e-13 | 5.4e-14 | −5.46e-13 | −5.46e-13 |
| 32x97 | +8.4e-14 | +1.08e-12 | 1.0e-12 | queued | queued |
| 32x101 (#145) | −1.27e-12 | −2.33e-12 | 1.1e-12 | −2.1e-14 | +1.5e-14 |

So far only 32x95 holds 1e-12 at D 60 by the criterion (`rt_grids.py --tol 1e-12` exits 0 there). Its neighbours miss on the other side of hp: 93 by +2.4e-12 to +2.8e-12, and 97 by +1.08e-12 from start b. The sign of the error alternates with each step of 2 in N from 89 to 97, inside an envelope that falls from 2.5e-11 at 89 to 6e-13 at 95. At 97 and 101 the spread of the two roots reaches 1e-12.

Added after these results, outside the verdict (reasons in `I164-mac/README.md`): 32x99 at D 60 from both starts, and 32x95 at D 60 from two more starts (the 97 and 93 roots), to see whether 95's root holds from the other side of hp. Next are the D 55 runs of 87 to 97, then 48x95 and the `--mutate=coef` control.

Raw commit d747d70. cpu: load 5.9, 45% idle (two RT processes of mine plus two of #106's). Memory: 31G used, 12G compressor, mine 0.9 to 1.4 GB each.

Progress, 2026-11-08 14:23 UTC (Mac).

All 28 solves of the criteria's grids are done, 85 to 97 at both D from both starts, and every one converged. Values are Δ_RT − Δ_hp (hp's double-double rows, err 2e-15). The spread is Δ_b − Δ_a of the two roots, a lower bound on how far the grid leaves Δ undetermined.

| N | N mod 4 | D 55: a | D 55: b | D 55 spread | D 60: a | D 60: b | D 60 spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 85 | 1 | +1.89e-10 | +1.89e-10 | −2e-20 | −3.42e-11 | −3.42e-11 | −1.0e-15 |
| 87 | 3 | −8.65e-11 | −8.65e-11 | | −5.24e-11 | −5.24e-11 | +2.2e-15 |
| 89 | 1 | +2.88e-11 | +2.88e-11 | +8e-19 | +2.58e-11 | +2.51e-11 | −7.1e-13 |
| 91 | 3 | −8.32e-12 | −8.32e-12 | +1.2e-16 | −8.37e-12 | −8.37e-12 | +2.3e-15 |
| 93 | 1 | +2.20e-12 | +2.20e-12 | +9.4e-16 | +2.35e-12 | +2.81e-12 | +4.6e-13 |
| 95 | 3 | −5.46e-13 | −5.46e-13 | −1.1e-16 | −6.38e-13 | −5.85e-13 | +5.4e-14 |
| 97 | 1 | +1.25e-13 | +1.25e-13 | −5e-17 | +8.4e-14 | +1.08e-12 | +1.0e-12 |
| 101 (#145) | 1 | −2.1e-14 | +1.5e-14 | +3.6e-14 | −1.27e-12 | −2.33e-12 | −1.1e-12 |

Two findings.

The truncation splits the odd N into two families by N mod 4. The sign of the error is (−1)^((N−1)/2) on 87 to 97 at both D. Within a family it falls about a decade per step of 4 in N, and it changes by less than a factor 1.7 from D 55 to 60. I wrote the sign rule into the raw README at 14:02 UTC (raw commit cc8728c), before the results of 87 at D 60 and of 87, 89, 93 and 97 at D 55. All five came out as it said. 85 at D 60 breaks it.

The spread of the roots also depends on the family. At D 55 it is 1e-15 or less on every grid. At D 60 it stays at 5.4e-14 or less for N ≡ 3 mod 4 (87, 91, 95), but reaches 4.6e-13 to 1.1e-12 for N ≡ 1 mod 4 from 89 on (89, 93, 97, 101). #145's ladder (81, 101, 121, 141) is entirely N ≡ 1 mod 4. This is a discrepancy with section 10's reading that refinement makes Δ worse from D ≈ 40. I will report it, not fix it.

So far the verdict is yes, on one grid: 32x95 at D 60. 32x97 misses only by its second root (+1.08e-12), so the cause there is the spread, not truncation. A second prediction, also in the raw README (commit 9d6d3e1), is that 32x99 (N ≡ 3 mod 4) holds at D 60 at about −5e-14 to −1e-13. It runs next, with two more starts for 95. Then come the pair test (does the residual rise between the two roots, which would make them distinct roots), the 48x95 control (running) and the `--mutate=coef` control (running).

Raw commit 71be7b4, wip/i164 at 078770f. cpu: load about 5.5, about 45% idle (my two RT processes and #106's two). Memory: 31G used, 12G compressor, my processes 0.9 to 1.4 GB each.

Closing summary, 2026-11-08 14:57 UTC (Mac, a subagent of the coordinator). Raw folder `I164-mac/` at raw commit 515578c (`raw_check.py` exit 0). The code and notes are on branch `wip/i164` at 72907e9. The write-up is section 11 of `notes/RT_FORMULATION.md`.

**Verdict: yes.** 32x95 holds Δ to 1e-12 at D 60.001952. Its values are −6.38e-13 (start a) and −5.85e-13 (start b), its two roots are 5.3e-14 apart, and `rt_grids.py --D 60.001952 --tol 1e-12` exits 0. No other grid of 85 to 97 passes. Two checks outside the criteria back it up. 32x99 holds as well (−3.45e-13 and −2.70e-13, exit 0). 32x95 re-solved from two more starts (the roots of 97 and 93) gives −6.37e-13 and −6.39e-13.

**What ran.** The criteria went into the raw README (commit c1f1669) before the main runs, and they were not changed afterwards. Options were #145's for D 55 to 60, with `--newton_tol` 1e-38 at D 55 and 1e-36 at D 60. Start a is #145's 32x101 continuation state, start b its 32x121 root, each resampled to the grid. The rule written beforehand added 87, 89, 93 and 97 (the smallest E, 6.4e-13 at 95, was below 1e-11, and E was not monotone in N). All 28 solves of the criteria (85 to 97, both D, both starts) converged, in 4 to 7 Newton steps and 104 to 316 s each, with a peak of 1.3 GB. Each `rt_run.py` exits 1 whenever |Δ − Δ_hp| > 1e-12, as designed: that is every grid except 95 at D 60 and 97 at D 55. Worker scripts: `run_main.sh`, `run_queue.sh`, `run_extra.sh`, `run_extra_a.sh` and `run_checks.sh`.

**Table.** Δ_RT − Δ_hp is the difference to hp's double-double row (up10 and up13, err 2e-15). The spread is Δ_b − Δ_a of the two roots, a lower bound on how far the grid leaves Δ undetermined, not an error bar.

| N | N mod 4 | D 55: a | D 55: b | D 55 spread | D 60: a | D 60: b | D 60 spread | verdict at D 60 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 85 | 1 | +1.89e-10 | +1.89e-10 | −2e-20 | −3.42e-11 | −3.42e-11 | −1.0e-15 | exit 1 |
| 87 | 3 | −8.65e-11 | −8.65e-11 | +2.0e-14 | −5.24e-11 | −5.24e-11 | +2.2e-15 | exit 1 |
| 89 | 1 | +2.88e-11 | +2.88e-11 | +8e-19 | +2.58e-11 | +2.51e-11 | −7.1e-13 | exit 1 |
| 91 | 3 | −8.32e-12 | −8.32e-12 | +1.2e-16 | −8.37e-12 | −8.37e-12 | +2.3e-15 | exit 1 |
| 93 | 1 | +2.20e-12 | +2.20e-12 | +9.4e-16 | +2.35e-12 | +2.81e-12 | +4.6e-13 | exit 1 |
| 95 | 3 | −5.46e-13 | −5.46e-13 | −1.1e-16 | **−6.38e-13** | **−5.85e-13** | +5.3e-14 | **exit 0** |
| 97 | 1 | +1.25e-13 | +1.25e-13 | −5e-17 | +8.4e-14 | +1.08e-12 | +1.0e-12 | exit 1 |
| 99 (extra) | 3 | | | | −3.45e-13 | −2.70e-13 | +7.5e-14 | exit 0 |
| 101 (#145) | 1 | −2.1e-14 | +1.5e-14 | +3.6e-14 | −1.27e-12 | −2.33e-12 | −1.1e-12 | exit 1 |

**What the table shows.**

The truncation splits the odd N into two families by N mod 4. From 87 to 97 the sign of the error is (−1)^((N−1)/2), at both D. Within a family it falls about a decade per step of 4 in N, and between D 55 and 60 it changes by less than a factor 1.7. I wrote the sign rule into the raw README at 14:02 UTC (commit cc8728c), before the results it named. It named five signs (87 at D 60, and 87, 89, 93 and 97 at D 55), and all five came out as named.

The new pair test in `rt_roots.py` finds two distinct roots at D 60 on 89, 93, 95, 97 and 99. The residual at the midpoint is 1.8e-28 to 8.6e-25, against about 2e-31 at the roots. On 85, 87 and 91, and on every grid at D 55, any pair is hidden by that floor. The pairs differ along section 4's weak direction (μ and harmonic 0 of ω₂, ω₃ and ω₄, spread over ξ). For N ≡ 1 mod 4 (89, 93, 97, 101) they are 4.6e-13 to 1.1e-12 apart in Δ. For N ≡ 3 mod 4 (95, 99) they are 10 to 20 times closer. So 97 misses at D 60 because of its pair, not its truncation.

**Controls.**

| control | expected | result |
|---|---|---|
| `--mutate=coef`, 32x91 at D 60 | Δ moves > 1e-6, exit 1 | Δ moved 1.31e-2, exit 1 (20 Newton steps, not converged, as in #145) |
| `rt_grids.py --mutate=shift`, 32x95 at D 60 | exit 1 | exit 1 |
| `rt_roots.py --mutate=same` | exit 1 | exit 1 |
| `rt_roots.py --mutate=mid` (the planted check of the pair test) | exit 1 | exit 1 |
| 48x95 − 32x95 from start a at D 60 (`nt_check.py`) | < 1e-13 | +1.5e-16, exit 0 (12 Newton steps, 26 min, 2.5 GB) |
| the same check with tol 1e-17 | exit 1 | exit 1 |

**Discrepancies (reported, not fixed).**

1. Section 10's reading, that refinement makes Δ worse from D ≈ 40, rests on one family. Every grid of #145's ladder (81, 101, 121, 141) has N ≡ 1 mod 4. In the N ≡ 3 mod 4 family, 95 and 99 hold 1e-12 at D 60. Nobody has measured whether that family keeps converging past 99. Its gain from 95 to 99 at D 60 is only a factor 2.
2. 10.9's proposed README sentence ("closes for 10⁻¹² near D = 60") needs the qualification in 11.7, which carries the replacement text.
3. The issue's premise, that the horizon branch makes the roots non-unique, does not explain why the pair separation depends on N mod 4. Section 11.4 offers a hypothesis: the family-dependent sign of the truncation pushes the system toward a fold or away from it. That has not been tested.
4. My prediction for 32x99 (raw commit 9d6d3e1) was right about the sign and the spread but wrong about the size: −2.7e-13 to −3.5e-13, against a predicted 5e-14 to 1e-13.
5. 32x85 at D 60 breaks the sign rule, and its error flips sign from D 55. I found no cause.
6. Two checks were wrong on their first run and were redone. `nt_check.py` first compared 48x95 against 32x95's D 55 record (it failed with 1.45e-2) and now matches on D. The c97 check ran before its solve had finished (`run_checks_c97.sh` redid it). Both are recorded in the raw README.
7. hp's rows are not in question. The closest RT values lie on both sides of them.

**Recommended tasks.**

1. *RT on the N ≡ 3 mod 4 ladder, D 40 to 60.* What: 32xN for N = 99, 103, 107, 111, 115, 119 and 123 at D = 40.020065, 50.007491, 54.996085 and 60.001952, two starts each, with `rt_roots.py`'s pair test. Why: section 10's conclusion about refinement comes from N ≡ 1 mod 4 alone, and this decides whether the other family converges, and where it stops. Acceptance (can fail): write the criteria first. At each D the family passes if |Δ − Δ_hp| falls along the ladder until it is below 1e-14, with both roots within 1e-14. Otherwise report the N and the value where it stops. `rt_grids.py --mutate=shift` and `rt_roots.py --mutate=mid` must exit 1. Depends on #164.
2. *Continue past D 60 on N ≡ 3 mod 4.* What: from the D 60 roots of 32x95 and 32x99, steps of 1 (cubic predictor) to D = 64.994829, the hp double-double row, then 70, with two-start re-solves on 95, 99 and 103 at the check D. Why: this shows whether the 1e-12 window that #145 reported as closing at D 60 stays open in this family. Acceptance: |Δ − Δ_hp| < 1e-12 at 64.994829 on some N ≡ 3 mod 4 grid from both starts, or the miss is reported. `--mutate=coef` at 64.99 must exit 1. Depends on task 1's criteria, or on #164 alone.
3. *For #163:* measure the pair separation max|z₂ − z₁| and the strength max|B(e,e)|/max|e| (11.4) on 93 to 99 at D 60, with and without rows that impose regular horizon behaviour. That turns the fold hypothesis into a test. It fits inside #163 rather than needing a separate task. Depends on #164.

The `running` label is removed and the issue is left open for review.

Coordinator review. I reran `rt_grids.py` on the 32x95 roots at D 60.001952 (exit 0, −6.38e-13 and −5.85e-13), its `--mutate=shift` (exit 1), and `rt_roots.py` on the 32x95 pair (exit 0). `raw_check.py I164-mac` exits 0 at 515578c. Merged into main as 455835e (rt_roots.py's pair test, notes/RT_FORMULATION.md section 11).

Verdict: yes. 32x95 holds Δ within 1e-12 of hp at D 60, and so does 32x99, which was run outside the criteria. No other grid from 85 to 97 does. The error splits by N mod 4, and section 10's conclusion that refining makes Δ worse rests on the N ≡ 1 mod 4 family alone. That is recorded as a discrepancy in section 11.

The recommended tasks: 1 is #166, 2 is #167, and 3 is a comment on #163.
